title: AI Warning Sends Nvidia, AMD, Micron and Intel Shares Tumbling
detail:
AI Warning Sends Nvidia, AMD, Micron and Intel Shares Tumbling
Nauman Khan
Mon, September 14, 2026 at 2:09 PM CDT 1 min read
NVDA
MU
AMD
INTC
AVGO
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and other major semiconductor stocks moved lower Monday as investors weighed calls from AI executives for a more measured approach to developing advanced systems.

Nvidia fell 2% in morning trading, while Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) dropped 5%. Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) declined 5%, Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) slipped 3.4%, and Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) lost 5.7%, extending weakness across several parts of the chip sector.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 4 Warning Signs with NVDA.

Is NVDA fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

NVDA GF Value chart

The selling followed comments from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who argued that progress in AI model capabilities should proceed at a slower pace because of potential risks. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman backed the need to pace development, while Elon Musk also supported Amodei's position.

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has similarly supported deliberate progress focused on AI safety, while Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis has previously favored coordinated measures if risks increase.

The comments add a fresh risk factor for semiconductor investors after a period of heavy spending tied to AI infrastructure. The market reaction suggests concerns over the pace and direction of AI development may be affecting sentiment toward chipmakers.

Broadcom's AI revenue surged 221% year over year with a forward P/E of 19, making it cheaper than Nvidia despite a similar growth trajectory.

TSMC revenue rose 53% year over year at a forward P/E of 20, and Dell booked a record $61B in AI orders last quarter.

On a recent Earn Your Leisure episode, hosts Troy Millings and Rashaad Bilal split openly on where the next dollar of AI value accrues. Millings argued for names outside the Magnificent 7 and made Broadcom's custom accelerator business the centerpiece of the case. Bilal countered that "you have to go with the people who are on the leaderboard," naming Taiwan Semiconductor (NYSE:TSM), Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), Micron (NASDAQ:MU), Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL), Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG, NASDAQ:GOOGL), Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), and the Nasdaq 100.

Ksw Photographer / Shutterstock.com

I find Millings the more persuasive of the two. Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) posted AI semiconductor revenue of $16.7 billion in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, up 221% year over year, and guided the fourth quarter to $21.7 billion, up 236%. On the earnings call, Hock Tan sketched a trajectory to roughly $115 billion in fiscal 2027 and $230 billion in fiscal 2028.

Those are company figures. They reframe what the phrase "alternative to Nvidia" means in practice.

Where the Earn Your Leisure Hosts Split

Millings framed the moment by saying, "The leaderboard is growing. You're looking at more trillion-dollar companies than we've ever seen before." His practical claim was that investors misread Broadcom's custom silicon and reflexively equate AI with Nvidia.
